outcomes.text: Understand short recordings about everyday needs, including simple transactions, directions and instructions.
Identify main points, specific information and details about everyday subjects.
Understand factual information and ideas from announcements, messages, news, interviews and dialogues on familiar topics.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Understand simple descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions.
Work out the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Understand short, simple texts such as public signs, notices and instructions.
Identify main points, specific information and details in predictable written texts.
Understand authentic texts about familiar topics and situations, including articles, emails, blogs and letters.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Understand simple written descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Take part in brief social exchanges and communicate about familiar topics to meet basic needs.
Use suitable strategies to keep an interaction going.
Hold unprepared conversations about familiar personal-interest and everyday subjects.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to communicate meaning and attitude.
Describe past events and experiences, hopes and ambitions, giving short reasons for opinions and plans.
Connect shorter points into a sequence using simple linking words.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied relevant structures, tenses and vocabulary.
Complete forms with simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Write linked phrases and sentences about personal life, immediate surroundings and everyday topics.
Produce connected texts about familiar subjects such as arrangements, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Link shorter written elements into a connected sequence using simple connectors.
Describe past events and experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, with brief reasons.
Write with reasonable accuracy using varied relevant structures, time frames and vocabulary.
Know and understand vocabulary and language relating to everyday activities, including time, food, health, travel and transport.
Know and understand vocabulary and language relating to personal and social life, including family, home, clothing, colours and leisure.
Know and understand vocabulary and language relating to people, places, nature, technology, the built environment, measurements and materials.
Know and understand vocabulary and language relating to education, training, jobs, careers and workplaces.
Know and understand vocabulary and language relating to countries, nationalities, languages, culture, customs, faiths and celebrations.

units.title: A Activités de la vie quotidienne

outcomes.text: Know vocabulary for months, years, dates and frequencies such as annual, monthly and weekly.
Know the four seasons and related seasonal vocabulary.
Know vocabulary for meals, courses, snacks, vegetarian food, picnics and barbecues.
Know common fruit vocabulary, including tropical and stone fruits.
Know vocabulary for common vegetables, including potatoes, salad vegetables and mushrooms.
Know vocabulary for staple foods, ingredients, dairy products, grains, seasonings and alternatives such as tofu.
Know vocabulary for meat, fish, seafood, sausages, hamburgers and poultry.
Know vocabulary for snacks and light meals such as sweets, crisps, cake, pizza, soup and sandwiches.
Know vocabulary for alcoholic-free drinks, hot drinks, water, juices, milk and ice.
Know vocabulary for plates, bowls, pans, cutlery, cups and glasses.
Use expressions and verbs for hunger, thirst, eating, drinking, preparing food, snacking and describing food as raw.
Use adjectives describing food as cooked, spicy, fresh, salty or sweet.
Know vocabulary for major body parts, including limbs, organs, facial features, skin and bones.
Use verbs for seeing, touching, smelling, breathing, shaving and applying make-up.
Know vocabulary for healthcare professionals, medicines, pharmacies, appointments and basic medical supplies.
Describe illnesses, injuries, symptoms, fitness, exercise, dieting, recovery and actions such as vomiting or falling.
Know vocabulary for transport, passengers, tickets, stations, journeys, luggage, vehicles, routes and tourism.
Use verbs and expressions for travelling, driving, boarding, arriving, departing, changing direction, parking and getting lost.
Use common greetings, farewells, apologies, thanks, requests, introductions and expressions about wellbeing.
Use exclamations expressing welcome, interest, annoyance, kindness and disappointment.
Invite someone, accept or refuse invitations, suggest activities and give polite reasons for declining.
Know vocabulary for family members, relationships, marital status, ages, generations and personal names.
Use verbs for having relatives, being pregnant, raising children, spelling names, growing up, being born, dying and living.
Describe people’s age, build, height, hair, eyes, complexion, facial hair, clothing accessories and physical characteristics.
Describe personality, behaviour, mood and emotional states using a range of positive and negative adjectives.
Express affection and emotions through verbs for liking, kissing, crying, laughing, smiling and becoming angry.
Know vocabulary for rooms, structural features and common household furniture.
Know vocabulary for bathroom fixtures, toiletries, cleaning items and personal-care objects.
Describe bathing, showering, brushing teeth and hair, washing the face and combing hair.
Know vocabulary for living-room furniture, furnishings and decorative objects.
Know vocabulary for kitchen containers, furniture and fixtures.
Describe cooking methods and kitchen activities, including boiling, frying, grilling, roasting, chopping, ironing and preparing meals.
Know vocabulary for bedroom furniture, bedding and storage.
Describe sleeping, waking, resting, lying down, getting up, feeling tired and feeling sleepy.
Discuss household chores such as vacuuming, washing clothes and dishes, cleaning, tidying, recycling and taking out rubbish.
Know vocabulary for gardens, plants, flowers, lawns, trees, fences and garden walls.
Describe gardening activities such as planting flowers, gardening and encouraging plants to grow.
Know vocabulary for household appliances, utilities, electrical items, controls and devices.
Describe operating, opening, closing, breaking, repairing, switching on and switching off household appliances.
Know common colour vocabulary, including light, dark, metallic and neutral colours.
Know vocabulary for clothing, footwear, jewellery, bags, accessories, sizes and materials.
Discuss fit, style, size, trying on, wearing, dressing and undressing clothes.
Discuss concerts, festivals, theatre, online chatting, music and different types of films.
Know vocabulary for musical instruments and hobbies including drawing, reading, gardening, fishing, painting and photography.
Know vocabulary for sports, sporting equipment, facilities, teams, competitions, players, supporters and activities.
Describe training, scoring, winning, losing, drawing matches and taking photographs.

units.title: C Le monde qui nous entoure

outcomes.text: Know the names of the world’s continents and major continental regions.
Give a candidate’s nationality, country of residence, first language, other studied languages and a Francophone country.
Know and use the four cardinal directions.
Know vocabulary for agriculture and natural features, including air, branches, fields, waterfalls and the sky.
Know French vocabulary for common animals, including pets, farm animals, insects and wild animals.
Know French words for weather and climate, including temperature, precipitation, storms, wind, snow and sunshine.
Use common French expressions to describe cold, heat, cool conditions, freezing and rain.
Know vocabulary for digital devices, online communication, social media, files, websites, passwords and internet safety.
Use verbs and expressions for accessing, navigating, creating, editing, sending, saving and downloading digital content.
Know French vocabulary for documents and texts, including books, forms, letters, tickets, magazines and identity cards.
Know vocabulary for buildings and public services, including schools, homes, shops, hospitals, leisure facilities and workplaces.
Know French words for urban areas, transport locations, roads, traffic facilities, public spaces and neighbourhoods.
Know vocabulary for shopping, including shops, prices, payment, customers, sales, sizes, money and refunds.
Use French verbs and expressions for shopping, buying, paying, spending, renting, returning goods and making complaints.
Know French units and terms for measurement, including length, weight, volume, temperature and distance.
Use French adjectives to describe size, height and length, from very small to enormous.
Know French vocabulary for geometric shapes and descriptions such as square, circular, round and triangular.
Know French words for common materials, including wood, cotton, leather, wool, metal, paper, plastic, glass and stone.
Know vocabulary for educational institutions, including nursery, primary and secondary schools, colleges, boarding schools and universities.
Know French vocabulary for education and training, including school staff, students, facilities, courses, terms and qualifications.
Know vocabulary for classrooms and school equipment, including furniture, stationery, books, computers, boards and bins.
Know French names for school subjects, including sciences, languages, humanities, arts, technology, sport and religious studies.
Know vocabulary for studying and school life, including lessons, homework, examinations, tests, projects, marks, breaks and results.
Use French verbs and expressions for learning, studying, revising, answering questions, taking notes, sitting and passing exams.
Know French vocabulary for a wide range of occupations and careers, including professional, skilled, public-service and creative jobs.
Know vocabulary for employment and workplaces, including businesses, offices, unemployment, salaries, employees, employers, work and CVs.
Use French expressions for applying for jobs, internships, promotion, dismissal, retirement, leave, unemployment and finding work.

outcomes.text: Know how to state a candidate’s nationality, country of residence, mother tongue, other studied languages and a Francophone country.

topics.title: La culture / les coutumes / la religion / les fêtes

subtopics.title: La culture / les coutumes / la religion / les fêtes

outcomes.text: Know vocabulary for religious beliefs, places, ceremonies, customs and festivals, including Christmas, Easter, Ramadan, Diwali and New Year.
Use French verbs and expressions for celebrating festivals, holding religious practices and expressing belief or religious observance.
